extra.message: commandJobHandler(String param) assigns the raw job parameter to `command` and passes it directly to Runtime.getRuntime().exec(command) with no validation or allow-listing. Any principal able to configure/trigger this XXL-Job task (admin console operator or reachable executor callback) achieves arbitrary OS command execution.

httpJobHandler parses a fully attacker/operator-supplied `url` parameter out of the job param string and opens an HttpURLConnection to it with no host/IP allow-list or protocol restriction, then returns the fetched content. Allows the job executor to be used as an SSRF proxy into internal networks.

The `/api/{uri}` OpenAPI endpoint (executor registry/registryRemove/callback) only validates the access token when `getAccessToken()` is non-blank. If `xxl.job.accessToken` is left unset, the check is silently skipped and executor registration/job-result callback is wide open to spoofing.

The only active gateway-level GlobalFilter declares the X_ACCESS_TOKEN header constant but never reads or validates it; it only rewrites the path and blanks the Authorization-UserName header before forwarding every request downstream. No path whitelist or signature/JWT check exists at the gateway tier, so auth enforcement is delegated entirely to (possibly missing) downstream checks.

createHttpClientWithNoSsl() builds an HttpClient using a X509TrustManager whose checkServerTrusted/checkClientTrusted methods are no-ops, disabling all TLS certificate validation. getStValidate() (line 41) uses this client to send the CAS ticket-validation request, so a network MITM can intercept/forge the CAS ticket-validation response and log in as an arbitrary user.
`/sys/actuator/memory/info` has no @RequiresPermissions/@RequiresRoles, unlike virtually every other controller in this codebase. Any authenticated user can read JVM/physical memory internals.

None of `/sys/actuator/redis/{info,metrics/history,keysSize,memoryInfo,queryDiskInfo}` carry @RequiresPermissions. queryDiskInfo discloses host disk layout/paths and getRedisInfo discloses Redis internals to any logged-in user regardless of role.

sendAll/sendUser push arbitrary attacker-supplied `message` text to all connected websocket clients or a chosen userId, with no permission annotation. Any authenticated user can spoof system broadcast/direct messages to any other user.
Every CRUD endpoint (add, edit, delete, deleteBatch, importExcel) lacks @RequiresPermissions, letting any authenticated user create/modify/delete arbitrary SysMessage records.

add/edit/delete/deleteBatch on SysMessageTemplate have no @RequiresPermissions, so any authenticated user can write arbitrary templateContent. This chains directly into the FreeMarker SSTI sink in PushMsgUtil.sendMessage, giving an unprivileged authenticated user a path to remote code execution via sendMsg.

sendMessage() builds a FreeMarker Template directly from sysSmsTemplate.getTemplateContent() (a DB-stored value writable via SysMessageTemplateController, which lacks auth checks) and calls template.process() with no sandboxing of the FreeMarker Configuration. A template containing `<#assign ex="freemarker.template.utility.Execute"?new()>${ex("id")}` executes server-side code when the template is rendered.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: The entire /sys/api/** controller (~90 endpoints) has zero @RequiresPermissions/@RequiresRoles annotations, unlike the rest of the audited modules. Compiled into the jeecg-system-biz business jar, so in a monolithic deployment these paths are reachable like any other controller endpoint.

sendEmailMsg, sendHtmlTemplateEmail, sendSmsMsg accept arbitrary email/phone/title/content/template parameters with no authorization check, usable as an open spam/phishing relay through the platform's own mail/SMS sender.

queryTableDictItemsByCode/queryFilterTableDictInfo forward raw table/filterSql request parameters into sysBaseApi dict-query methods with no authorization annotation despite a comment implying signature verification exists.
checkSignature() compares the MD5 signature using signature.equals(md5(...)), a non-constant-time string comparison, enabling a timing side-channel against the OpenAPI secret key.

corsConfiguration.setAllowCredentials(true) combined with addAllowedOriginPattern("*") registered for "/**". addAllowedOriginPattern (unlike addAllowedOrigin) is accepted together with allowCredentials(true) by Spring, so any origin can issue credentialed cross-origin requests and read JSON responses from the entire API.

extra.message: preHandle() reflects the client-supplied Origin header verbatim into Access-Control-Allow-Origin (httpServletResponse.setHeader(ACCESS_CONTROL_ALLOW_ORIGIN, httpServletRequest.getHeader(ORIGIN))) and sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true, when allowOrigin (default true) is enabled. This independently compounds the WebMvcConfiguration CORS misconfiguration at the Shiro filter layer, allowing any origin to make credentialed requests.

extra.message: checkSsrfHttpUrl (used by FileDownloadUtils.openSafeConnection / download2DiskFromNet / getDownInputStream, i.e. uploadImgByHttp/URL-download code paths) only rejects loopback and link-local addresses; isSiteLocalAddress() (RFC1918 10.x/172.16.x/192.168.x) is never checked, by explicit design per the comment at line 329-330. An attacker who controls a download URL can make the server fetch from arbitrary internal/private-network hosts.

`public static String key = "1234567890adbcde"; public static String iv = "1234567890hjlkew";` are hardcoded in source and consumed by AesEncryptUtil.resolvePassword for login password decryption. Since the key/IV are fixed and visible in source, this provides no real confidentiality against an active attacker who reads the code.

extra.message: `props.put("spring.datasource.dynamic.druid.wall.selectWhereAlwayTrueCheck", false);` explicitly disables Druid's firewall heuristic that flags `SELECT ... WHERE <always-true>` patterns (classic ' OR '1'='1 payloads) at JDBC level, removing a defense-in-depth layer against any SQL injection that reaches the datasource.

Signature scheme is MD5(json(params) + secret) (DigestUtils.md5DigestAsHex) rather than a keyed HMAC such as HMAC-SHA256. MD5 is cryptographically broken and this secret-suffix construction is weaker and less reviewed than HMAC.
